name: FILTER
description: FILTER extracts rows from a range that meet a condition, returning a dynamic array of matching results. It's the array-era replacement for complex IF/INDEX combinations.
tldr: FILTER pulls out matching rows from a table based on a condition. Unlike VLOOKUP (which returns one value), FILTER can return entire rows and multiple matches — all in one formula.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array to filter. Can be a single column or a multi-column table.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: A Boolean array (TRUE/FALSE) of the same height as the array. TRUE rows are included, FALSE rows are excluded.

parameters.name: if_empty
parameters.description: The value to return when no results match the filter. Default is #CALC!.

basicExample.description: Filter a product table to show only items in the 'Electronics' category
basicExample.result: Shows all electronics rows (name, price, category, stock)
basicExample.explanation: C2:C50="Electronics" creates a TRUE/FALSE array. FILTER keeps only rows where the category is 'Electronics' and spills the matching rows.

advancedExamples.title: Multiple condition filter (AND logic)
advancedExamples.description: Filter for Electronics items priced under $100
advancedExamples.explanation: Multiply conditions with * for AND logic. TRUE×TRUE=1 (included), TRUE×FALSE=0 (excluded). Both must be TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: Multiple condition filter (OR logic)
advancedExamples.description: Filter for items that are either 'Electronics' OR 'Books'
advancedExamples.explanation: Add conditions with + for OR logic. TRUE+TRUE=2, TRUE+FALSE=1, FALSE+FALSE=0. >0 means at least one condition is met.

advancedExamples.title: FILTER with custom empty message
advancedExamples.description: Return 'No results found' when the filter produces no matches
advancedExamples.result: No results found (if no furniture exists)
advancedExamples.explanation: The third argument replaces the #CALC! error with your custom message when no rows match.

howItWorks: FILTER works by creating a Boolean mask over your data. The 'include' argument evaluates each row against your condition, producing an array of TRUE/FALSE values. Rows where the result is TRUE are kept; FALSE rows are dropped. The remaining rows spill into adjacent cells as a dynamic array. For multiple conditions, multiply (*) for AND logic or add (+) for OR logic — this converts TRUE/FALSE to 1/0, allowing math-based combination.

howToSteps.name: Select the data range
howToSteps.text: Choose the full table or column you want to filter (e.g., A2:D50).

howToSteps.name: Define the condition
howToSteps.text: Write a condition that produces TRUE/FALSE for each row: C2:C50="Electronics", B2:B50>100, etc.

howToSteps.name: Combine conditions if needed
howToSteps.text: Use * for AND: (cond1)*(cond2). Use + for OR: (cond1)+(cond2)>0.

howToSteps.name: Set empty result text
howToSteps.text: Add a third argument like "No results" for when no rows match.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =FILTER(range, condition, empty_text) in a cell with enough space below for spilled results.

limitations: FILTER is only available in Excel 365 and Excel 2021+ — not in earlier versions.
Results spill into adjacent cells — those cells must be empty or you'll get a #SPILL! error.
FILTER returns all matching rows — there's no built-in way to limit to top N results (use SORT + INDEX for that).
Large datasets may slow down recalculation since FILTER re-evaluates on every change.

commonErrors.cause: No rows match the filter condition and no if_empty argument was provided
commonErrors.fix: Add a third argument: =FILTER(range, condition, "No results") to display a custom message instead of the error.

commonErrors.cause: Filtered results need to spill into cells that already contain data
commonErrors.fix: Clear the cells below and to the right of the FILTER formula to give it room to spill results.

commonErrors.cause: The include array has a different number of rows than the data array
commonErrors.fix: Ensure both arrays have the same height. If data is A2:D50 (49 rows), include must also span 49 rows.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets has FILTER with the same syntax and behavior, plus it's available in all versions.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Google Sheets FILTER has been available longer than Excel's. It works identically. In Sheets, you can also use QUERY for SQL-like filtering.

faq.question: How do I filter with multiple AND conditions?
faq.answer: Multiply conditions: =FILTER(A2:D50, (C2:C50="Electronics")*(B2:B50<100)). Both must be TRUE for a row to be included.

faq.question: How do I filter with multiple OR conditions?
faq.answer: Add conditions and check >0: =FILTER(A2:D50, (C2:C50="Electronics")+(C2:C50="Books")>0). At least one must be TRUE.

faq.question: Can FILTER return just one column?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the array to a single column: =FILTER(B2:B50, C2:C50="Electronics") returns only the prices of electronics.

faq.question: Does FILTER work in Excel 2019?
faq.answer: No. FILTER requires Excel 365 or Excel 2021+. In older versions, use INDEX/MATCH or VLOOKUP for similar (but less powerful) functionality.

faq.question: How do I sort filtered results?
faq.answer: Wrap FILTER in SORT: =SORT(FILTER(A2:D50, C2:C50="Electronics"), 2, -1) filters electronics and sorts by price descending.
